# `network/peerTickets/PeerTicket.js`

> **Source:** `engine/network/peerTickets/PeerTicket.js`

network/peerTickets/PeerTicket.js — encrypted, remembered reconnect records (network plan §38).  A peer ticket is a signed statement "peerId X is reachable, offers these services, at these route hints, valid until Y" — it lets a device reconnect to known peers/groups without the discovery server, once trust has already been established once. Sealing (encrypting the ticket itself) reuses the same ECDH-wrap pattern as group welcome packets (engine/network/groupCrypto/GroupEpoch.js), OR a group's current encryption epoch directly, per network plan §38 "encrypt to recipient device key OR group epoch key".

### `async verifyPeerTicket(signedTicket, { now = Date.now()`

Verify a peer ticket: known protocol/type, not expired, signature valid.

**Returns:** >}

### `async sealPeerTicketToDevice(signedTicket, recipientEcdhPublicKeyRaw)`

ECDH-wrap a signed ticket so only the holder of `recipientEcdhPublicKeyRaw`'s private key can read it.

### `async openSealedPeerTicket(sealed, recipientPrivateKey)`

Recipient side: unwrap a device-sealed ticket. Returns null (fails closed) on any error.

### `async sealPeerTicketToEpoch(groupCrypto, epoch, signedTicket)`

Seal a ticket under a group encryption epoch (readable by any member with that epoch's key).

### `async openSealedPeerTicketFromEpoch(groupCrypto, envelope)`

Open an epoch-sealed ticket. Returns null if the epoch key is missing/erased or tampered.
